liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Liberty** (2 reviews): Reviewer judges this the best Liberty ever played; Described as the first and best Liberty, played with Garcia's acoustic-sounding MIDI patch [10][11]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): A woman in the crowd is audible on tape, happily calling it one of her favorites [8]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): The audience was hushed during Garcia's solo; reviewer calls it a favorite guitar solo ever [15]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Eternity [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-02-21.138697.sbd.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 150 min [1]
- **gd93-02-21.aud.seff.1055.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 148 min; rated 4.3/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience noise is prominent on the recording and adds to the fun; Reviewer describes the sound as great and acoustic-leaning [8][16]
- **gd1993-02-21.fob.copeland.evans.GEMS.86058.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 152 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1993-02-21.132376.sbd.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended in Oakland and was startled by new songs, despite expecting little from nineties Dead shows [5]
- Reviewer drove from Yosemite to Oakland that day and heard several new songs [10]
- The band had just come off a month away from touring [12]
- Three new songs were played well, with Garcia especially strong and no sign of later decline [14]
- Reviewer recalls a reverent atmosphere in the arena that night [15]
- Reviewer sat in the first row of seats on Garcia's side, with a clear view, after driving from Humboldt [16]
- Garcia used the acoustic MIDI sound on many songs here, and it stayed in use for many shows that year [11]
- This audience recording is much better than the other one then available [12]
- A newer audience source is said to sound better than this one [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-02-21.138697.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Dat (44.1k) [1]. Also: Soundboard source credited to Miller, distributed as FLAC [1]
- **gd93-02-21.aud.seff.1055.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jon Seff; source: Audience: Unknown Mics [2]
- **gd1993-02-21.fob.copeland.evans.GEMS.86058.flac16**: taped by Chip Copeland; transferred by DAT Clone from Dat Master from collection of Todd Evans Editing Info- All editing and mastering by Jamie Waddell; source: Neumann km140 (110 deg. ORTF) -> Neumann Supply -> Panasonic sv255 [3]
- **gd1993-02-21.132376.sbd.flac16**: source: SBD> DAT> Steve Block CAS master> DAT> CDR> Sequoia 11-> WAV [4]
